- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 3–7% if recent price is falling.  
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day); cap forecast at 10–15% above prior peak.  
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, forecast should not drop below 10% below recent low.  
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates in early period (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; add 1–3% to forecast for first 5 days.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows, model tends to lag; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead if sentiment is trending.
